main_text.p: quisquis resistit Potestati, dei ordinati-oni resistit.] Chryfostomo adiungere liceret illud nobile doctorum par, Hieronymum & Augustinum, duo magna Occidentalis Ecclesiae luminaria; quorum ille de Dauidis poenitentia post cumulatum adulterio homicidium loquens, eum dixisse ait: Tibi soli peccaui quia Rex erat, & alium non timebat. Quod idem planius & plenius S. Ambrosius in sua Apologia pro Dauid, vt antea, explicaui-mus. Aut igitur Dauid qua Rex erat, nullum nisi Deum superiorem agnoscebat, cui supplicium dare deberet: aut falso & arroganter, Deo soli se pec-casse iactitabat. Hoc autem viro, caeteris pio prudentique & diuinitus etiam afflato, abfit impingamus; neq; abfi-milis illa{x} Xiphil. in Dione, in vi-ta Marci Anton. philosophi. Regis Philosophi leni ac placido ingenio Principis ab hac Regis Prophetae vox, Nemo nisi solus Deus, iudex principis esse potest. Finio cum testimonio Beati Augustini, qui praeter allegationes (ab eius scriptis in superiori-bus citatas) in duabus Epistolis oftendere satagit, persequutionem Tyranno-rum esse probationem iustorum, nec a Deo

page.notes: Long s read as plain s throughout; the old "f"-like forms were not transcribed as f. Greek-looking initial N in "Nemo" (italic) is uncertain: transcribed as Nemo, possibly an ornamented capital. The reference mark "x" after "illa" is printed in the text, but no matching mark is visible in the margin note; the note is placed at that point. Left edge strip shows part of the neighbouring page and is excluded. Printed hyphens at line ends kept as printed. "abfit impingamus" and "neq;" are as printed.
